summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex history of mesenteric fibromatosis, chronic abdominal pain, and TPN dependence was admitted directly from GI clinic due to severe, uncontrolled pain and malnutrition after discontinuing home TPN for three weeks. She was restarted on hospital TPN with improved tolerance and nutritional support. Pain management was optimized through consultation with the chronic pain service, including a trial of Dilaudid PCA, followed by multiple medication adjustments, ultimately transitioning to methadone. A new left thigh hematoma was identified, associated with supratherapeutic anticoagulation from home Lovenox; it was managed conservatively with dose reduction to prophylactic levels, warm/cold compresses, and a lidocaine patch. Her nausea improved, anemia was monitored, and she remained stable without active bleeding or infection. She was discharged home with services on adjusted pain and anticoagulation regimens, new TPN formula, and follow-up plans.
